title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and follow directions, take a rickshaw or bus, and give polite and informal instructions.
intro: The auto-rickshaw (**રિક્ષા**) is the classic way to get around Gujarati cities, along with city buses and Ahmedabad's BRTS and metro. This unit teaches the **imperative** — how to tell someone to go, stop or turn — in its intimate, polite and extra-polite forms, plus the case endings for 'to', 'from' and 'up to'.

vocab.en: to get off/out; to go down
to sit; to get on (a vehicle)
up to, until, as far as

vocab.note: n · બસ (f) 'bus' is spelled like બસ 'enough'; the state bus is ઍસ.ટી. 'S.T.'
f · Ahmedabad's river is the સાબરમતી

phrases.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
How far is it from here?
Bhai, will you go to Manek Chowk? (to a rickshaw driver)
How much will the fare be?
Does this bus go to Gandhinagar?

phrases.roman: māre āvtā sṭop par ūtarvuṃ chhe.
phrases.en: I want to get off at the next stop.

grammar.title: The imperative: three levels
grammar.body:
Gujarati commands change with the level of politeness:

**Intimate (તું):** bare stem — **જા** 'go', **આવ** 'come', **બેસ** 'sit', **વળ** 'turn'.
**Polite (તમે):** stem + **-ઓ** — **જાઓ, આવો, બેસો, વળો**. This is the normal form with adults.
**Deferred / extra polite:** stem + **-જો** — **જજો, આવજો, બેસજો, વળજો**. It sounds softer and often refers to later ('do turn right when you get there'). Intimate version: **-જે** (આવજે).

Negative commands use **ના / ન** before the verb, or the -શો + નહીં form for politeness: **ત્યાં ના જાઓ** 'don't go there', **ચિંતા કરશો નહીં** 'please don't worry'.

examples.en: Turn right at the second lane. (polite, deferred)

grammar.title: Direction and location: -એ, -થી, સુધી, તરફ
grammar.body:
Gujarati usually needs **no word for 'to'** with places: **હું બજાર જાઉં છું** 'I'm going to the market'. Many place nouns can also take the locative **-એ** for 'to/at': **ઘરે** 'home', **શાળાએ** 'to school', **સ્ટેશને** 'to/at the station'.

**-થી** *-thī* means 'from' (also 'by' a means): **અમદાવાદથી** 'from Ahmedabad', **અહીંથી** 'from here', **બસથી** 'by bus'.
**સુધી** means 'up to, as far as, until': **સ્ટેશન સુધી** 'as far as the station'.
**તરફ** means 'towards': **નદી તરફ** 'towards the river'.

Put them together: **અહીંથી ત્યાં સુધી** 'from here to there'.

examples.native: હું રોજ બસથી ઑફિસ જાઉં છું.
examples.roman: huṃ roj basthī ofis jāuṃ chhuṃ.
examples.en: I go to the office by bus every day.
The children have gone to school.
How much is the fare to the station?

examples.native: આ રસ્તો મંદિર તરફ જાય છે.
examples.roman: ā rasto mandir taraf jāy chhe.
examples.en: This road goes towards the temple.

examples.native: વડોદરાથી સુરત સુધી ટ્રેનમાં બે કલાક થાય છે.
examples.roman: Vaḍodarāthī Surat sudhī ṭrenmāṃ be kalāk thāy chhe.
examples.en: From Vadodara to Surat takes two hours by train.

dialogue.title: Taking a rickshaw
dialogue.setting: Lisa flags down an auto-rickshaw outside Ahmedabad's Kalupur railway station.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.en: Bhai, will you go to Law Garden?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: Yes, get in. By meter or fixed price?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: ઠીક છે. તમારે ક્યાં ઊતરવું છે?
lines.roman: ṭhīk chhe. tamāre kyāṃ ūtarvuṃ chhe?
lines.en: OK. Where do you want to get off?

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.en: Near Law Garden, opposite the bank.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: પુલ પર બહુ ટ્રાફિક છે. બીજા રસ્તે જઈએ?
lines.roman: pul par bahu ṭrāfik chhe. bījā raste jaīe?
lines.en: There's a lot of traffic on the bridge. Shall we take another road?

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.en: All right. But please drive a bit slowly!

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: આ રહી બેંક. અહીં ઊભી રાખું?
lines.roman: ā rahī beṅk. ahīṃ ūbhī rākhuṃ?
lines.en: Here's the bank. Shall I stop here?

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.native: હા, અહીં બરાબર છે. કેટલા થયા?
lines.roman: hā, ahīṃ barābar chhe. keṭlā thayā?
lines.en: Yes, here is fine. How much is it?

culture: Rickshaw drivers in Ahmedabad are usually addressed as **ભાઈ** or **કાકા**. Directions are given by landmarks rather than street names — a temple, a bank, a famous sweet shop or a **ચાર રસ્તા** — so it's normal to ask several people along the way. **આ રહ્યું / આ રહી** means 'here it is'.
